issues: Scene omits that Jesus also commands the disciples to cease praying aloud while continuing to pray in their hearts (3 Nephi 20:1).
The summary's phrase “Jesus truly gives them both” could imply an unmentioned means of provision; the source confirms the gift but does not describe how it is provided (3 Nephi 20:6–7).
The preceding scene identifies the speaker as Jesus and the listeners as the multitude; labeling them unnamed loses that established continuity.

The dialogue excerpt “Behold now I finish the commandment” is not contiguous: the source continues “which the Father hath commanded me concerning this people, who are a remnant of the house of Israel.” Use an exact contiguous excerpt.
The dialogue excerpt from verse 12 omits the intervening words “then is the fulfilling of the covenant which the Father hath made unto his people, O house of Israel.” Use an exact contiguous excerpt.

The explicit fact says the Father promises to establish Israel “in this land as a New Jerusalem,” but verse 22 says “this people” will be established in this land and “it shall be a New Jerusalem”; clarify the referent rather than assert the conflated wording as direct fact.

The dialogue excerpt “A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren” omits the continuation “like unto me; him shall ye hear in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you.” It is not a contiguous verse excerpt as supplied.
The dialogue excerpt in verse 31 omits “and shall pray unto the Father in my name,” so it is not a contiguous excerpt of the supplied sentence.

The dialogue excerpt “Sing together, ye waste places of Jerusalem” is not contiguous with its beginning in verse 34: “Then shall they break forth into joy—”. Quote a complete contiguous phrase from the supplied text.
The dialogue excerpt “Awake, awake again, and put on thy strength, O Zion” omits the continuation in verse 36; use an exact contiguous excerpt.
The dialogue excerpt “Thy God reigneth!” omits the preceding words in the same quoted sentence and is not contiguous with the excerpt as supplied; use a contiguous excerpt.
The summary describes the servant's visage as marred, but does not make clear this is quoted prophecy rather than a present event; preserve the teaching-only chronology.
